scenarios.prompt:
I'm building a leaderboard and need to rank these 5 items fairly, accounting for sample size (I don't want a single 10-star rating to beat an item with 800 reviews averaging 8.7). Use a shrinkage constant of 100 phantom votes, with the global mean computed from the items themselves.

  A: avg_rating=9.6, n=5
  B: avg_rating=8.7, n=850
  C: avg_rating=9.1, n=42
  D: avg_rating=7.2, n=1500
  E: avg_rating=10.0, n=1

Report top_bayesian_avg (top-ranked item's shrunken score) and rank_of_A (1 = best).

Same 5 items (A 9.6/5, B 8.7/850, C 9.1/42, D 7.2/1500, E 10.0/1). I want the ranking to be less conservative - let smaller-sample items move faster toward their observed average. Drop the shrinkage constant to 20 phantom votes. Report top_bayesian_avg and rank_of_C.

One of our items has a single 10-star review. The site-wide average across all items is 7.5. Using a shrinkage constant of 50 phantom votes, what's this item's effective rating for ranking purposes? Report bayesian_avg.
